name: Seven Rocks
description: Seven Rocks is a four-player partnership domino game in the Fives family. Players build a cross-shaped layout, score when open ends total a multiple of five, and race to 250 points.

overview.description: Seven Rocks is a four-player partnership domino game in the Fives family. Players build a cross-shaped layout, score when open ends total a multiple of five, and race to 250 points.

history.origins: Seven Rocks is a Fives-family domino game that became popular in California and the Southwestern United States, where tournament and book publication helped standardize play.
timeline: 2001: Seven Rocks rules and strategy notes first published online.
2020: Rule conventions and naming updated in published sources.
Current: Played as a partnership race to 250 with single-spinner mechanics.

setup.players: Exactly 4 players in fixed partnerships (partners sit opposite).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 7 tiles; all tiles are dealt, so there is no boneyard.
setup.equipment: Domino set and running score tracker (cribbage board or score sheet).

rules.objective: Be the first partnership to reach 250 points by making the open ends of the cross-shaped layout total a multiple of five when possible and by minimizing hand-end pip penalties.
rules.gameplay: Lead any tile. Players in turn must match an open end; if no match is possible they pass. The first double played is the only spinner and creates the cross-style expansion pattern. After each play, score immediately if exposed ends total 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 or 30. A hand ends when someone dominoes or all players are blocked. Then each player's remaining pips are rounded to nearest five and subtracted from that player's score.
keyRules: Only the first double is a spinner.
No boneyard exists in Seven Rocks.
Passing is required when no legal tile can be played.
If the previous hand was blocked, the next opening lead is determined by lot.

strategy.basic: Prioritize legal plays that create immediate multiple-of-five scoring totals.
strategy.intermediate: Use spinner branch choices to shape which pip values remain open for both teams.
strategy.advanced: Track unplayed tiles and force passes while preserving your team’s scoring-end tempo.
tips: Doubles can swing scoring because exposed double ends count their full pip totals.
In blocked positions, leave ends your partnership can still support.

scoring.description: Score immediately when exposed ends total a multiple of five. At hand end, each player's remaining pips are rounded to nearest five and subtracted from that player's score.

synthesis.shortDescription: Seven Rocks is a four-player partnership domino game where only the first double is a spinner and scoring comes from open-end totals that hit multiples of five.
